title: Azure Monitor Logs query results truncate at 30,000 rows
answers: Why does my Azure Monitor Logs query only return 30,000 rows?
Logs panel shows a notice that the row limit was reached
How do I disable the Azure Monitor Logs row limit?
Azure Monitor logs results truncated / cut off
body:
Symptom: an Azure Monitor query using the Logs result format returns exactly 30,000 rows even though more data exists, with a UI notice that the limit was reached.
Root cause: the Logs result format renders every row at once in the frontend table, so the backend truncates to prevent the browser tab from crashing (pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor/loganalytics/azure-response-table-frame.go).
Fix pattern: gate the truncation behind a feature toggle so users can opt out when they accept the performance tradeoff, rather than hardcoding the limit unconditionally.
Constraints: only applies to the Logs result format (not time series/table-for-graph formats); opt-out is the `azureMonitorDisableLogLimit` feature toggle checked in pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor/loganalytics/azure-log-analytics-datasource.go. Recommend `summarize`/narrower time range/filters as alternatives to disabling it.
says: Why does my Azure Monitor logs query only return 30000 rows?
Logs panel shows a notice that the row limit was reached
How do I disable the Azure Monitor logs row limit?
Azure Monitor logs output is truncated or shows partial results
search: The Logs result format in Azure Monitor truncates at 30,000 rows (pkg/tsdb/azuremonitor/loganalytics/azure-response-table-frame.go) because the frontend renders every row without virtualization, creating crash risk. The truncation is gated by the azureMonitorDisableLogLimit feature toggle checked in azure-log-analytics-datasource.go, allowing opt-out while defaulting to safety. Only the Logs result format applies; time-series and table-for-graph formats are not truncated. Recommend alternatives like summarize, time-range narrowing, or filtering before users disable the limit.
